statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-54514 (GHSA-hgj6-7826-r7m5): jackson-databind deserialized java.net.InetSocketAddress with new InetSocketAddress(host, port), which resolves the host name during deserialization, so untrusted JSON bound into a type with an InetSocketAddress field could make the application send DNS queries for attacker-chosen names (server-side request forgery). com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind 2.0.0 to 2.18.7 and 2.19.0 to 2.21.3 are affected, and 2.18.8 and 2.21.4 fix it; the Jackson 3 artifact tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind is affected before 3.1.4. Advisory: https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson-databind/security/advisories/GHSA-hgj6-7826-r7m5. The 2.x fix is commit 1f5a103 on the 2.18 branch, from pull request 5951, which creates the address with InetSocketAddress.createUnresolved instead: https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson-databind/commit/1f5a1037b1e9e05920e755cb35f198bcd46667e4. The jackson-databind-2.18.8 tag contains it and jackson-databind-2.18.7 does not. This package is the Gradle 8 build tool, which bundles jackson-databind. We read every published gradle-8 package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, x86_64 and aarch64: 16 versions, 8.14.4-r0 to 8.14.8-r0, each matching its repository index checksum. 8.14.5-r4 is published for x86_64 only, and every aarch64 package has the same index checksum as its x86_64 package. Each package ships jackson-databind as /usr/share/java/gradle/lib/jackson-databind-<version>.jar, and its version comes from the Maven metadata inside the jar, not from the file name: 2.18.6 in 8.14.4-r0 to 8.14.5-r3, 2.18.8 in 8.14.5-r4 and 8.14.5-r5, 2.18.9 in 8.14.5-r6 to 8.14.5-r9, 2.18.11 in 8.14.6-r0 to 8.14.7-r0 and 2.18.12 in 8.14.8-r0. Each of these jackson-databind jars has the same SHA-256 as the jar of that version on Maven Central. The class files agree: com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/deser/std/FromStringDeserializer$Std.class has no reference to InetSocketAddress.createUnresolved in jackson-databind 2.18.6 and has one in 2.18.8, 2.18.9, 2.18.11 and 2.18.12. Each package has exactly one jackson-databind jar; no other jar in it, including jars nested inside jars, contains jackson-databind classes under any package prefix, and no package ships Jackson 3 classes under tools/jackson. The range ends at 8.14.5-r4, the first build with a fixed jackson-databind; 8.14.5-r3 and every earlier build carry an affected one.
